Everyone said "Hey Grok" was impossible on iPhone. Even Grok said Apple keeps wake words for Siri only. So I kept digging, and I found a way. Now I just say "Hey Grok" and Grok Bot voice chat opens. No extra apps, no cost, all built into iOS.

How to set it up:

1. Make sure your Grok Bot app is up to date

2. Shortcuts app → + → Add Action → search "Grok Bot" → pick "Start Voice Chat with Bot"

3. Settings → Accessibility → Vocal Shortcuts → Set Up → pick that shortcut → type "Hey Grok" and say it 3 times

4. In the shortcut's details, turn on "Allow Running When Locked"

If your phone is locked, iOS asks for one tap first. If Face ID already unlocked it, it's fully hands-free.

SpaceX’s $SPCX Starlink just surpassed AT&T $T Fiber in subscribers after tripling its customer base in just seven quarters. What’s even more impressive is that Starlink is adding roughly 1.6 million subscribers per quarter versus about 400,000 for AT&T Fiber — showing how much faster satellite networks can scale compared to laying fiber street by street.

Starlink’s connectivity CAGR sits at over 90% while AT&T Fiber manages around 17%. In a world racing toward AI / SI and orbital infrastructure, that gap isn’t just a statistic. It’s a structural advantage.

Image data courtesy of http://Fiscal.ai

The more I look at the economics of AI infrastructure, the more bullish I become on SpaceX.

David Sacks shared some fascinating numbers on All-In:

- SpaceX: ~$50B in monetization per GW, with roughly a 1-year payback.

- CoreWeave: ~$20B per GW, with roughly a 2.5-year payback.

These are estimates, but the difference is enormous.

A big reason is how the two companies structure their contracts.

CoreWeave relies heavily on long-term commitments to finance its infrastructure. SpaceX has the balance sheet and access to capital to operate with much shorter contracts, giving it exposure to today’s significantly higher compute pricing.

That flexibility is worth a LOT in a supply-constrained market.

And consider what happens when you’re recovering your capital in roughly a year. You can reinvest that money into additional compute, bring more capacity online, and potentially accelerate growth without relying as heavily on external financing.

Now consider SpaceX is targeting ~13 GW of operational compute capacity by the end of 2027.

The economics at scale could be extraordinary if they execute.

I’ve been extremely bullish on SpaceX for years, but the AI infrastructure opportunity has become a much bigger part of the investment thesis.

I remember sitting around a campfire shortly after the Ukraine war had just started with some Ukrainian friends.

They shared that after they learned that Russian forces were jamming all communications they called Elon begging for Starlink support.

Elon and the Starlink team instantly dropped everything they were working on, loaded a private jet with as many Starlink terminals as they could (terminals were in short supply at the time), and started flying the jet eastward while writing code to make terminals work over Ukraine.

There was no contract or promise of payment for doing so, and no time to solve for that.

My Ukrainian friends believed this saved the nation of Ukraine, and that without this effort Ukraine would have lost the war nearly instantly.
